hypotheses.name: Morgagni hernia with liver herniation
hypotheses.basis: Right paracardiac homogeneous opacity abutting diaphragm without air, preserving mediastinal position, consistent with intra-abdominal organ (liver) in anterior mediastinum through foramen of Morgagni

hypotheses.name: Diaphragmatic hernia with stomach herniation
hypotheses.basis: Less likely due to absence of air-fluid level or gastric bubble; however, a gasless stomach could mimic this—requires verification

hypotheses.name: Pericardial effusion
hypotheses.basis: Unlikely because cardiac silhouette is not globally enlarged/globular and left heart border remains sharp; effusions typically cause bilateral border obscuration or symmetric enlargement

discriminators.question: Which options describe a right-sided opacity directly contiguous with the diaphragm vs. pleural/parenchymal/pericardial?

discriminators.attribute: presence of air or air-fluid level
discriminators.question: Does the opacity contain air (suggesting stomach) or lack air (suggesting liver)?
Is there ipsilateral or contralateral mediastinal shift?
Are air bronchograms, lobar collapse, or peripheral infiltrates present?
Is the cardiac outline globular or preserved?
Is the opacity well-defined and homogeneous (organ) vs. irregular/multifocal (tumor)?

uncertainties: No clinical history (e.g., age, symptoms, prior imaging) provided
No lateral view to confirm anterior location of opacity
Cannot definitively distinguish liver vs. other solid viscus without contrast or CT
Exact diaphragmatic defect site (Morgagni vs. Bochdalek) not confirmable on PA CXR alone
